text:
mike: Heads-up — incoming customer ask: finance-analytics wants p99 <= 300ms for single-turn completions at 8k context. Product is pushing for p95 <= 150ms as the public SLA. How do we reconcile?
elaine: That's a tough one. p95 150ms is only achievable with tiny microbatches and aggressive KV cache hits. p99 300ms for 8k is realistic but depends heavily on kernel choice + IO.
kevin: Quick profiling yesterday showed a 2.6x difference between cuBLAS-based matmul and our fused attention kernel on their model at 8k. Tail spikes come from tokenization + KV cache restores on cold sessions.
sarah: Do we have numbers for different microbatch sizes? I ran continous-batch tests: mb=1 avg=120ms p95=160ms p99=420ms, mb=4 avg=220ms p95=260ms p99=480ms. These were on A10G with quantized weights.
mike: Oof. So microbatching helps throughput but kills tail. Product wants the 150ms p95 marketing number but sales are promising customers the p99 300ms.
carla: For customer-specific SLAs i'd prefer we offer two tiers: "low-latency" (p95 150ms, limited qps) and "high-throughput" (p99 300ms, higher qps). That maps to Dedicated pools + kernel pinning.
elaine: Agree. Implementation notes: kernel selection needs to be per-pool. We can prefer fused-attn for low-latency and switch to batched-matmul for throughput. Need to expose microbatch cap in route config.
kevin: Also KV cache behavior: cold-start of cache for long-context sessions adds 80-150ms depending on model size. We should pre-warm KV for reserved sessions or add a warmup API.
sarah: I pushed a small perf script to reproduce. Perf-bot recorded a regression yesterday when we rolled the new kernel selector. Perf-bot: regression detected on 1749871200 — p99 increased 1.12x on 8k trace.
perf-bot: @eng-runtime flagged: p99 latency regression at 8k context after canary. See /perf/runs/1749871200 for details.
mike: Thanks. Elaine/kevin can you triage kernel selector change? If we revert, we might lose throughput wins. We need a targeted rollback for only the fused-attn toggle.
elaine: I'll run A/B with kernel pin override. Quick experiment plan: 1) force fused-attn + mb=1 2) force batched-matmul + mb=4 3) fused-attn + mb=2 + prefix cache on. Collect p50/p95/p99 and tail histograms.
kevin: Also add CPU-side tokenization timings, and measure KV restore time per-slot. Put histograms in the trace so Product can see tradeoffs.
ikevin: (typo) meant kevin: ^
sarah: For customer conversation: we should present concrete numbers and a recommendation: "To meet p95 150ms we can do LowLatency mode with guaranteed reserved slots and reduced qps; otherwise p99 300ms in Standard mode."
mike: Sales/Product alignment question: are we comfortable promising p95 150ms as a public SLA? That constrains hosting configs.
carla: Not as a broad SLA. We can advertise achievable p95 for specific model/context combos and offer SLAs per-customer with Dedicated capacity.
elaine: Perf note: kernel selector knock-on effects — choosing fused-attn for short sequences helps latency but increases mem pressure for long sequences which hikes p99. So selector should consider seq-length histogram (not just avg).
kevin: Action items: kevin/elaine to run the A/B by EOD, sarah to compile a one-pager for Product+Sales with charts (p50/p95/p99, qps tradeoffs, recommended configs), mike to draft customer wording for SLA tiers.
mike: One-pager should include suggested fallback policy: if p99 > threshold then fall back to lower precision model variant or throttle. Also show cost delta.
sarah: Will include cost per 1M tokens for each config and expected latency curves.
carla: Good. For the customer ask (finance-analytics) propose: dedicated pool, pinned fused-attn, pre-warm KV, mb=1, and a 50 qps cap to guarantee p95 150ms, or Standard pool with p99 300ms at 400 qps.
mike: Perfect. If the experiments confirm numbers, we'll present to Product + Sales tomorrow.
elaine: Starting profiling now. I'll post results in this thread.
kevin: If experiments fail, fallback is to carve out a special image with an older kernel selector we know is stable.
sarah: Noted. Also adding a small sample trace we can share with the customer showing tail causes.
mike: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
elaine: Initial run done — fused-attn + mb=1: p95=148ms p99=295ms on their 8k trace. Uploading histograms.
sarah: Nice. That's within the proposed SLA if we limit qps and pre-warm.
mike: Great, let's lock the proposal and get Product/Sales signoff.
